name: An Egyptian, Café d'Egypte
bio: A waiter at the Café d'Egypte in Paris who, Wilde wrote to Leonard Smithers in September 1900, 'occasionally serves me drinks'. Wilde describes him as 'A slim brown Egyptian, rather like a handsome bamboo walking-stick', and says in the same sentence that he does not console him for the loss of a Neapolitan who had gone home. No name, age, dates or further trace appear on the page read.
bio_note: THE LABEL IS A DESCRIPTOR, NOT A NAME: the source preserves no name. 'An Egyptian, Café d'Egypte' is what the record provides - the nationality Wilde ascribes to him and the café where he worked - rendered as a node label; it must never be cited as though it were a name. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE RESEARCH BRIEF, BOTH confirmed in the source: (1) the recipient is LEONARD SMITHERS, not George Ives. The passage stands in Wilde to Leonard Smithers, [Postmark 2 September 1900], Paris; the letter to George Ives, [Postmark 6 September 1900], begins lower on the same printed page and contains nothing of the kind. (2) The café is in PARIS, not Cairo - it is named the Café d'Egypte and Wilde is writing from Paris, so the working label 'the Cairo-café Egyptian' is a misreading of the café's name. The id was therefore set to 'paris-egyptian' rather than the working brief's 'cairo-egyptian', to keep a false place-name out of the corpus; this can of course be reverted. Source: Complete Letters (2000), p. 1196 (repo PDF 1242, printed folio 1196 confirmed at the foot of the rendered page image, read 2026-08-03). PROVENANCE CAVEAT, from the editors' own footnote 1 on the same page: 'The text of this incomplete letter is taken from Forty Years in my Bookshop by W. T. Spencer (1923), corrected and supplemented by the American Art Association catalogue of 1 February 1928.' The heading carries no manuscript line - unlike the Ives letter below it, which is 'MS Texas' - so this text descends from a printed memoir and a saleroom catalogue rather than from a surviving manuscript, and the letter is incomplete. The letter states no age and none is inferred. A FURTHER DISTINCT PERSON IN THE SAME SENTENCE, NOW HIS OWN ENTRY: 'that brown faun with his deep woodland eyes and his sensuous grace of limb', also called 'the wanton sylvan boy of Italy' - one man under two epithets, and a different man from this one. Added as a person 2026-08-04; see brown-faun. The earlier pointer list had conflated the two under one heading. DATES: NONE RECORDED (2026-08-03). Searched so far: the whole OCR mirror of the Complete Letters (2000) for every occurrence of the name, plus the edition's General Index; Frankel, Oscar Wilde: The Unrepentant Years (2017), repo PDF, the fullest scholarly account of the exile years; McKenna, The Secret Life of Oscar Wilde (2008) and Murray, Bosie (2020), repo PDFs. Frankel quotes the same description at printed p. 271 (repo PDF 285) and gives no name or dates. ONE THING STILL TO CHECK: Frankel places the cafe inside the Egyptian pavilion of the 1900 Paris Exposition rather than at a standing 'Cafe d'Egypte' - worth checking against the letter before the node label is treated as settled. No birth or death date is recorded in any source consulted, and none is likely to be: the record preserves a first name (or a trade) in another man's correspondence and no surname to search by. That absence is itself the historical fact worth keeping - these men enter the written record only because Wilde wrote to his friends about them.
